text.arabic_uthmani: ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِى لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ وَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍۢ شَدِيدٍ

words.gloss_range: genitive proper divine name anchoring the ownership clause and, under the canonical local parse, completing the prior path chain while accepted case variation marks a possible restart
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field tied to deity, worship, seeking refuge, and debated derivation; the local word functions as the uniquely identified divine referent, not a generic deity noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) opens the ayah as the named divine referent, not an indefinite deity term; root discussions around worship, refuge, longing, and bewilderment remain relational pressure while the local word stays a proper name. In the local genitive reading it completes the prior path-chain across the boundary; the accepted nominative contrast would restart the sentence, so the case vowel matters for how the ayah begins. From that name, the clause expands into a familiar total-ownership formula also seen in related declarations (2:284; 20:6), then into judgment: the owner of the cosmic field is also the referent before whom denial and punishment are framed, with same-surah reprises later (14:8; 14:22).

topics.headline: case variant at the ayah boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the canonical genitive carries the prior path-chain across the ayah boundary, while the accepted nominative reading would restart the sentence.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support the genitive continuation locally, while the variant rows remain useful as a contrast in how the ayah can be heard.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ownership claim is made of the uniquely named divine referent, not of an indefinite deity category.
topics.reason: The local word is a definite proper noun, and the relative clause expands that named referent rather than introducing a generic title.

topics.headline: worship and refuge derivation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses a relational divine name whose root discussions involve worship, refuge, longing, or bewilderment, while local grammar keeps the proper name as the selected function.
topics.reason: The derivational rows are not allowed to replace the local proper-name function, but they preserve real lexical pressure around the divine relation being named.

topics.headline: divine ownership formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the following clause as a familiar total-ownership formula also seen in related declarations (2:284; 20:6).
topics.reason: The local syntax directly contains the divine name followed by the relative possession formula and the heavens-earth pair.

topics.headline: divine name anchors denial and punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the named owner of the cosmos also anchors the ayah’s denier-and-punishment field, later revisited in the surah (14:8; 14:22).
topics.reason: The same local ayah contains the divine name, denier class, and punishment noun, and the CRITICAL rows identify same-surah reprises with concrete references.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular definite relative pronoun that identifies the divine antecedent through the following ownership clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) turns the following possession clause into an identifier of the divine antecedent. Its masculine singular form keeps the clause attached to the named referent, not to the plural domains that will follow. Under the local genitive reading it works adjectivally, while the accepted nominative contrast can make the same relative material predicative. The relative span also delays the woe declaration until total ownership has first been stated.

topics.headline: relative clause identifies by ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the divine antecedent defined through possession rather than through a separate title.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word a masculine singular relative tied to the divine antecedent.

topics.headline: relative can route adjective or predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same relative word can either attach the ownership clause to the prior genitive chain or help make it a fresh predication under the variant reading.
topics.reason: The canonical local parse is adjectival to the preceding divine name, while the nominative variant supports the predicative contrast without controlling the base parse.

topics.headline: long ownership span before warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the warning delayed until after the owner has been characterized by total cosmic possession.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence has the relative material running through the earth phrase before the new woe sentence begins.

words.gloss_range: fronted possessive prepositional phrase with a divine suffix; locally marks exclusive ownership before the owned totality is named
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahū}}) puts the owner relation first. The suffix sends the phrase back to the divine name, while the fronted predicate makes possession by Him the organizing premise before the owned field is named. The lām is locally possession and specification, and the boundary rows let this total ownership ground the previous ayah’s authorization language.

topics.headline: suffix routes ownership to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one compact suffix keeps the divine referent present without repeating the name.
topics.reason: The preposition plus suffix is the fronted predicate for the owned set and refers back to the divine antecedent.

topics.headline: possession and specification in the lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase as possession and exclusive attribution, while local context rules out looser purpose readings.
topics.reason: The cosmic inventory selects possession and specification; other lām functions remain possible elsewhere but are not local.

topics.headline: fronted predicate foregrounds owner
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ownership by Him is placed first, before the inventory of owned things appears.
topics.reason: Word order makes the prepositional predicate precede its subject, giving the owner relation organizing force.

topics.headline: ownership grounds prior permission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the prior authorization language to total ownership at the ayah boundary.
topics.reason: The boundary row states that the possession claim supplies the basis for the permission language from the previous ayah.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun functioning as the owned-set subject after the fronted predicate; locally means whatever is within the first domain, not negation or question
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is the owned-set subject after the fronted predicate, not negation or question. It opens the first unrestricted whatever-in frame, so the phrase does not merely name the heavens but includes whatever exists within that domain across the rational and non-rational boundary. It also sets the slot that will be mirrored for the earth.

topics.headline: relative subject not negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the word as the subject of the owned set, not as a negating or interrogating particle.
topics.reason: The fronted predicate before it and locative phrase after it force the relative-pronoun parse.

topics.headline: whatever opens the owned field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owned field is left open-ended enough to include the whole contents of the domain.
topics.reason: The local relative pronoun functions as an unrestricted selector for the possessed set inside the first domain.

topics.headline: first slot of a mirrored frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader anticipates that the first whatever-in frame will be mirrored for the earth rather than collapsed into a bare pair.
topics.reason: The later coordinated phrase repeats the relative-pronoun slot while the predicate remains understood.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition governing the heavens and making the possessed set spatially contained within the upper domain
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the ownership claim locative. It governs the upper domain and turns the phrase toward what exists within that realm, not a causal or temporal relation. As the first fī, it also begins the parallel locative frame that will be repeated for earth.

topics.headline: locative containment of the upper domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ownership specified as whatever exists within the upper domain, not as abstract possession alone.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the heavens in a locative phrase and makes them the container-domain for the owned set.

topics.headline: spatial scope blocks other particle values
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the concrete domain sense while recognizing that temporal, causal, or instrumental values are not selected here.
topics.reason: The governed noun is the heavens, so local grammar selects spatial containment over other possible values of the particle.

topics.headline: compact first locative frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small particle starts the locative pattern repeated for earth, giving both domains the same ownership structure.
topics.reason: The first locative phrase is structurally mirrored by the second, preserving spatial symmetry.

words.gloss_range: definite plural upper domain governed by the first locative phrase; part of the heavens-earth totality under divine ownership
words.root_gloss_range: height and upperness field, with related naming/designation pressures; the local form selects the concrete plural upper domain within a cosmic ownership merism
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ}} ({{tr:al-samāwāti}}) is the definite plural upper domain inside that first locative frame. The word carries height and canopy pressure, and the root-family link with naming or designation adds ordered-domain pressure, but locally it functions as the concrete plural heavens. Paired with earth, it forms a formulaic totality rather than a casual list. Its first-half landing, stretched by long ā cadence, gives the upper domain its own full weight before the clause restarts for the lower domain, and the same pair later appears with creation language (14:19).

topics.headline: definite plural upper domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the heavens as a known, bounded plurality governed inside the ownership phrase.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place the definite plural noun as the genitive object of the locative preposition.

topics.headline: elevated domain with canopy pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the upper realm as elevated and enclosing, while local grammar keeps it a concrete plural domain rather than a free image of height.
topics.reason: Dictionary pressure supports height and canopy imagery, but the local form is the concrete plural heavens in a locative phrase.

topics.headline: elevation and naming derivation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a root-family pressure between elevation and designation, while the local word still selects the spatial heavens rather than a naming derivative.
topics.reason: The rows press a real derivational spread, but QAC and the local phrase select the concrete domain form.

topics.headline: heavens-earth totality formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the heavens-earth pair as a formulaic totality frame, not a casual two-item list.
topics.reason: The contextual profile shows the heavens-earth root pair as dominant, and the local syntax coordinates the two domain phrases.

topics.headline: same-surah cosmic thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ownership of the cosmic pair here as the opening of a same-surah thread later tied to creation (14:19).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify the same pair recurring later with creation language and boundary expansion from guidance into cosmic ownership.

topics.headline: upper phrase gets its own landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first domain land fully before the earth half restarts the pattern.
topics.reason: The word closes the first whatever-in unit, and the sound row supports the breadth of that first landing.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining two full mirrored whatever-in phrases into one totality claim
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge between two complete whatever-in frames. It joins the heavenly and earthly domains as coordinated assertions under one ownership predicate, rather than reducing them to two adjacent nouns. The visible fusion into the next word makes the second half both continuous and freshly started.

topics.headline: conjunction joins two full frames
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees two complete whatever-in frames coordinated, not merely two nouns strung together.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the second relative phrase with the first.

topics.headline: additive union of domains
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the conjunction as the hinge that turns upper and lower domains into one total owned field.
topics.reason: The conjunction links mirrored structures under the same understood ownership predicate.

topics.headline: visible restart in the written form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees continuation attached directly to the second relative pronoun rather than a detached new sentence.
topics.reason: The proclitic conjunction is visibly joined to the second relative slot in the source form.

words.gloss_range: repeated relative pronoun restarting the owned-set frame for earth while the possessive predicate remains understood
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) repeats the quantifier for the earth side while the possession predicate remains understood. That selective repetition keeps the two domains parallel: each receives its own whatever, and one owner governs both. The result is distributive totality without repeating the owner phrase.

topics.headline: second relative pronoun retained
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the earth domain receives its own explicit whatever even though the owner phrase is not repeated.
topics.reason: The second relative pronoun is explicit while the possession predicate is understood from the first half.

topics.headline: earth independently universalized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees totality distributed across each domain instead of compressed into a single heavens-and-earth label.
topics.reason: The repeated frame gives earth its own scope while one possessor governs both halves.

topics.headline: quantifier echo across the two halves
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second whatever as both attached to the first half and fresh in its own slot.
topics.reason: The fused coordinated form restarts the same mā-plus-locative structure.

words.gloss_range: repeated locative preposition giving earth its own containment relation parallel to the heavens
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) repeats the locative relation for earth. The second domain does not merely inherit the first preposition in a compressed pair; it receives its own containment phrase. The unchanged particle makes the two halves comparable and symmetrical.

topics.headline: earth has its own locative scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees earth separately scoped as a container-domain, not simply appended to the first locative phrase.
topics.reason: The second preposition governs the earth and repeats the containment relation locally.

topics.headline: same particle, same function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears structural symmetry because the identical particle performs the same locative work in both halves.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence gives both instances the same prepositional-complement function.

words.gloss_range: definite singular lower domain governed by the second locative phrase; completes the heavens-earth ownership merism
words.root_gloss_range: earth, ground, land, lower substrate, and territory field; the local pairing with the heavens selects the maximal lower-domain sense
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) closes the ownership merism as the definite lower domain. Its ground and substrate pressure makes it the lower pole opposite the elevated heavens, while the local pairing selects the maximal earth-domain sense rather than a local land parcel. The noun-only profile keeps earth as a stable object-domain, not an action or process, and the singular lower realm balances the plural heavens to complete the formulaic pair. Once this word lands, the ayah has expanded from the prior path into the cosmos and is ready to narrow into warning.

topics.headline: definite lower domain under the second preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees earth as a known lower domain governed within the same ownership syntax, not as another owner or a loose appendage.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place the definite noun as the genitive object of the second locative preposition.

topics.headline: ground and substrate pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the lower support-plane completing the vertical totality, while local pairing selects the maximal earth-domain sense rather than a local territory.
topics.reason: The root rows support ground, land, and substrate pressure, but the heavens pairing narrows the local sense to the lower cosmic domain.

topics.headline: stable noun-only earth field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices earth as a stable object-domain in the corpus, not an action or process.
topics.reason: The supplied distribution gives the local root as a concrete noun field, fitting its role as a contained domain.

topics.headline: earth completes the totality pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the singular earth balancing the plural heavens to complete the formulaic totality.
topics.reason: The dominant heavens-earth pair is locally coordinated under divine ownership.

topics.headline: ownership beat closes before warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the scale expand to the cosmos and then prepare to narrow sharply into the woe clause.
topics.reason: The word closes the ownership beat before the resumptive woe sentence begins.

words.gloss_range: resumptive or lightly coordinating conjunction that pivots from completed cosmic ownership to a new woe declaration
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots after a complete ownership clause. It can still link the warning to sovereignty, but locally it opens a fresh woe sentence rather than adding another descriptor to the divine name. The turn is abrupt: cosmic possession has just been completed, and the discourse moves immediately to doom.

topics.headline: new sentence after ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a discourse break from ownership declaration into warning rather than another descriptor of God.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence treat the following woe material as a new nominal sentence after the ownership clause.

topics.headline: coordination still links warning to sovereignty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the warning connected to the sovereignty claim, while the local syntax still marks a fresh speech act.
topics.reason: The previous clause is complete, so restart is strong; the particle can still carry linkage without collapsing the clauses.

topics.headline: immediate pivot into woe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah turn abruptly from cosmic scope to declarative doom.
topics.reason: The transition is fused to the woe noun and begins the construction unit for the warning.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative doom noun, functioning as exclamation or nominal subject, then routed to recipients and source
words.root_gloss_range: doom, grief, calamity, destructive harm, and warning-formula field; the local clause selects declared ruin directed to a class and sourced in punishment
words.prose: {{ar:وَيْلٌۭ}} ({{tr:waylun}}) launches the warning as an indefinite doom noun. Its form allows cry-like exclamation and nominal-sentence force, then the following phrases route that doom to a target and a source. The lexical range includes grief, destruction, and failed refuge pressure, but the local clause selects a doom verdict aimed at deniers and answered by severe punishment. The word converts the preceding ownership claim into evaluative consequence and joins a warning formula where woe, denial, and punishment recur together elsewhere (41:6-7; 83:1-10); the falling sound shape reinforces the cry-like force.

topics.headline: open-ended doom noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices doom declared as an open state before its recipients and source are specified.
topics.reason: The local noun is nominative and indefinite, then receives target and source complements.

topics.headline: cry-like and sentence-like force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears both an exclamatory doom cry and a nominal sentence capable of assigning that doom.
topics.reason: The nominative form licenses exclamation or subject-like parsing with the following target phrase.

topics.headline: grief, destruction, and failed refuge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels ruin and failed refuge pressure, while the local target and punishment phrase select doom rather than mere sorrow or an independent place-name claim.
topics.reason: Dictionary range is narrowed by the local denier target and severe-punishment source.

topics.headline: woe turns theology into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ownership claim converted into evaluative consequence for the deniers.
topics.reason: The woe noun launches the second beat after the completed ownership frame.

topics.headline: formulaic link to denial and punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a warning formula in which woe, deniers, and punishment are brought together, with related pairings elsewhere (41:6-7; 83:1-10).
topics.reason: The local clause contains all three fields and the CRITICAL rows identify concrete formula parallels.

topics.headline: woe expands into target and source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees an exclamation become a routed judgment through a target phrase and a source phrase.
topics.reason: The construction unit scopes over the denier target and severe-punishment source together.

topics.headline: sound supports cry-like force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the falling sound shape reinforce the exclamatory function without replacing the lexical meaning.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows add a concrete acoustic payoff to the already licensed woe exclamation.

words.gloss_range: targeting preposition that assigns the woe to the denier class before the source phrase appears
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) directs the doom. Here the lām does not mark possession for the deniers but assignment against them: first the warning names whom the woe reaches, then the min phrase names what it comes from. The small preposition turns a free exclamation into a governed judgment.

topics.headline: lām assigns woe to the deniers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the doom aimed at a governed class rather than left as a free cry.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the denier noun and supplies the target complement for the woe noun.

topics.headline: designation against, not possession for
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same lām family has shifted from possession for the divine owner to disadvantage assigned against the deniers.
topics.reason: Local context selects target or disadvantage assignment here, not beneficial ownership.

topics.headline: target frame precedes source frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the warning in order: first whom the woe reaches, then what punishment it comes from.
topics.reason: The lām phrase precedes the min phrase, creating a two-preposition frame around the woe declaration.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participle naming the recipients as an ongoing class of coverers or deniers
words.root_gloss_range: covering and concealment field extended to denial, unbelief, ingratitude, repudiation, and related cover-images; the local active participle selects the condemned denier class
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ}} ({{tr:al-kāfirīna}}) names the recipients as a definite active-participle class, characterized by ongoing covering or denial rather than a single past act. The root’s covering image makes denial feel like active concealment set against the disclosure of total ownership, while local grammar selects the condemned denier sense rather than neutral covering or atonement branches. The ayah narrows from all that is in the heavens and earth to this morally charged class; it also converts the previous ayah’s darkness-to-light movement into human agents of concealment. The word ties them to a dense denial-punishment field that returns later (14:7; 14:22) and opens a same-surah polemical thread.

topics.headline: known class named by ongoing action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the recipients as a recognized class characterized by continuing denial or covering, not merely by a past event.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a definite masculine plural active participle governed by the targeting preposition.

topics.headline: covering image under denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels denial as active covering set against the preceding disclosure of total ownership, while local context selects the condemned denier sense.
topics.reason: The root rows support concrete covering imagery, but the local active participle and woe target select theological denial.

topics.headline: evaluative recipient of woe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the cosmic ownership frame narrowing onto a morally charged human class.
topics.reason: The denier phrase is the governed target of woe after the universal ownership claim.

topics.headline: broader covering family kept in bounds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root family’s range across concealment and covering-over, while local context blocks atonement or neutral covering from replacing denial.
topics.reason: The broader family is real but local targeting by woe selects the condemned concealment pole.

topics.headline: formulaic denial-punishment pairing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes deniers and punishment as a dense Quranic pairing made local in this woe clause.
topics.reason: The local clause contains the denier class and punishment phrase, and the CRITICAL rows identify same-surah returns (14:7; 14:22).

topics.headline: darkness becomes concealer agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the previous ayah’s darkness-to-light movement with this class of coverers.
topics.reason: The boundary rows map the prior darkness condition into the human class named by covering.

topics.headline: same-surah polemical thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this first denier label as opening a polemical thread that later returns in the surah.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row tracks repeated k-f-r material through Surah 14.

words.gloss_range: source, cause, or specification preposition linking the woe declaration to the punishment phrase
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) bridges the woe to its source or specification. It can carry cause, origin, or explanation, but in this construction it keeps the punishment phrase attached to the woe declaration rather than letting it float as a new event. After the target phrase, this second preposition supplies the warning’s source frame, and its nasal sound binds closely to the following indefinite punishment noun.

topics.headline: source or explanation of woe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment phrase explaining and generating the woe, not floating as a separate event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence has the particle governing the punishment noun as the source or cause of the woe.

topics.headline: scope between woe and denier relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a real scope question, while the construction unit keeps the source phrase tied to the woe declaration.
topics.reason: The source phrase may be heard in relation to the woe or doomed relation, but attachment evidence treats the whole warning as one nominal construction.

topics.headline: one particle pivots from target to source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the second preposition as the bridge from whom the woe reaches to what it comes from.
topics.reason: The lām phrase gives target first, and this particle gives the source or specification before the punishment noun.

topics.headline: sound binds particle to punishment noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the small particle tied acoustically to the following indefinite punishment noun.
topics.reason: The sound row supplies a concrete nasal link between the particle and the governed noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite abstract punishment noun governed by the source preposition and qualified by severity; the kind remains open while the force is intensified
words.root_gloss_range: punishment and torment field with prevention or deterrent pressure and a contrasting sweet-water root-family pole; the local noun selects punitive consequence under the source phrase
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابٍۢ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābin}}) gives the warning its content as an indefinite abstract punishment. Its kind is left open while the following adjective fixes intensity and locks severity to the punishment itself, not to the deniers or to woe as a separate noun. Its genitive government under min makes it the source or specification of the woe, and the nominal form presents punishment as a source-state behind the declaration rather than a finite event with an overt agent. Root-family pressure from sweetness and prevention sharpens the reversal, but local grammar selects punitive consequence, later reprised in the severe-punishment formula (14:7).

topics.headline: open punishment intensified by adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the kind of punishment remains unspecified while its severity is fixed.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an indefinite abstract noun, and attachment evidence binds the following severity adjective to it.

topics.headline: punishment as source of woe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees punishment functioning as the generating source or specification of the woe.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the source preposition and supplies content for the warning tail.

topics.headline: severity locked to punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees severity attached to punishment itself, not to the deniers or to woe as an independent noun.
topics.reason: Agreement and attachment evidence bind the adjective to the punishment noun.

topics.headline: sweetness and prevention pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels a sharp root-family reversal from sweetness toward punitive prevention, while local grammar selects punishment as the operative sense.
topics.reason: The root rows preserve sweet-water and prevention pressure, but the source phrase and severity adjective select the punitive pole.

topics.headline: abstract noun instead of event verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment presented as a source-state behind the woe rather than as a finite event with an overt agent.
topics.reason: The local form is an abstract noun, not a causative finite verb or a punished-person participle.

topics.headline: punishment-severity and denial field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the severe-punishment formula and its same-surah reprise in direct warning (14:7).
topics.reason: The local noun is paired with the severity adjective and denier class, with concrete same-surah echo rows.

topics.headline: final phrase completes warning architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final punishment phrase complete the warning by giving source, quality, and consequence field.
topics.reason: The phrase supplies the source and quality without becoming a separate clause.

words.gloss_range: genitive indefinite adjective bound to the punishment noun; marks stable, constrictive severity and closes the ayah
words.root_gloss_range: tightening, binding, strengthening, firmness, intensity, and severity field; the local adjective selects punitive severity while retaining constrictive pressure
words.prose: {{ar:شَدِيدٍ}} ({{tr:shadīdin}}) closes the ayah by binding severity to the punishment noun. The adjective pattern gives stable intensity, while the root’s tightening and binding pressure makes that severity feel constrictive. Its indefinite ending keeps the punishment phrase open-ended rather than pointing to a known named punishment, and the wording joins a standard punishment-severity bond. Because it is the final word, the warning lands not merely on punishment but on punishment marked as severe; the same force thread returns with punishment (14:7) and destructive wind (14:18), while sound, doubled consonant pressure, and tanwīn reinforce the closure.

topics.headline: severity grammatically bound to punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word as a dependent qualifier of punishment, landing after the noun it intensifies.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the adjective as agreeing with and qualifying the punishment noun.

topics.headline: durable intensity in the adjective form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices severity as a stable quality of the punishment, not a passing action.
topics.reason: The faʿīl adjective pattern and local attributive position support durable intensity.

topics.headline: binding and tightening pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels severity as constrictive tightening, while the local collocation selects punitive severity rather than every strength-related branch.

topics.headline: open-ended indefinite qualifier

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated construction 'to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth.'
baseline_models.mechanism: The deity is the personal pole of possession, while the overhead canopy and its lower counterpart form a vertically exhaustive field. Repeating 'whatever is in' assigns every contained entity to that one relation, so the warning is issued from within an owned domain rather than from outside it.

activation_trace.role: The worshiped deity supplies the personal center to whom the exhaustive possession is assigned.
What rises and overshadows supplies the upper containing canopy of the owned field.
The lower realm opposite the sky completes the vertical totality of possession.

changed_reading.before: God is associated with the heavens and earth, and disbelievers face punishment.
changed_reading.after: Every being is already situated inside God's vertically exhaustive possession, so the woe is an owner's judgment within a domain from which no creature stands outside.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The noun 'the disbelievers' follows immediately after the exhaustive ownership formula.
baseline_models.mechanism: The covering image in kufr makes the named group functional rather than merely taxonomic: they cover truth, blessing, or the visible claim of the owner while remaining inside the very field they cover. The juxtaposition creates an irony of attempted concealment under total possession.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the act by which the owned field's disclosure is occluded.
Blocking truth specifies the epistemic object of the covering.
Covering a benefit keeps ingratitude live as a second object of the same act.
The elevated and conspicuous image makes the attempted covering occur against a visibly manifest field.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers are a doctrinal class threatened after a statement of sovereignty.
changed_reading.after: They are coverers operating inside an already manifest and wholly owned field, concealing truth or benefit without escaping the owner's claim.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The compact phrase 'from a severe punishment' joins the roots ع ذ ب and ش د د.
baseline_models.mechanism: Alongside direct pain, the ع ذ ب inventory carries potable sweetness and restraint or deprivation, while ش د د carries fastening and hard force. Coactivation makes severity a tightly imposed withdrawal of relief, not merely a higher score of pain.

activation_trace.role: Pain and punitive injury provide the explicit base event.
Sweet potable intake supplies the relief whose inversion makes the punishment anti-refreshment.
Restraint and deprivation supply the withholding operation within the pain.
Fastening and binding turn severity into a constraint that holds its subject.
Force and hardness preserve the ordinary intensifying sense while giving it material pressure.

changed_reading.before: The punishment is simply very painful.
changed_reading.after: The punishment may work as forcefully tightened deprivation: relief, intake, and release are withheld while pain is held in place.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening gives revelation a downward delivery that extracts people from concealment into illumination; the next ayah describes the disbelievers as diverting people from an extended path and bending its meaning. Kufr in the focus is therefore active resistance to a supplied movement of disclosure, not only a settled interior opinion.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the obscured state from which the opening movement seeks extraction.
Causing something to descend and arrive supplies the delivered intervention.
Bringing something out of concealment gives the intervention its uncovering direction.
Light and illumination provide the disclosed destination opposed to covering.
Turning aside supplies the counterforce that interrupts the offered exit.
An extended traversable road makes disclosure a course that can be blocked.
Deviation of meaning supplies deliberate distortion in addition to simple obstruction.

structural_cues: 14:1 runs directly into the focus through the destination 'path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.'
14:3 immediately expands the focus noun into present actions: preference, obstruction, and pursuit of crookedness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies descent, extraction, illumination, path obstruction, and semantic bending; I infer that these actions unpack kufr as countermovement against disclosure. A live alternative is that the movement imagery and the legal warning remain adjacent but independent.

changed_reading.before: Kufr is a static covered state followed by punishment.
changed_reading.after: Kufr is a counter-process that resists being brought out, blocks others on the owner's path, and bends the route away from illumination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus triad of kufr, punishment, and severity recurs inside an explicit contrast between recognizing benefit and receiving increase. The next ayah scales kufr to everyone on earth yet declares God self-sufficient. Severe punishment therefore answers the recipient's covering of benefit; it does not repair a lack in the owner.

activation_trace.role: Recognition of a benefit and praise of its giver supplies the positive alternative to kufr.
Increase and growth make gratitude a reception channel that can be enlarged.
Covering a benefit directly identifies the focus coverers as ungrateful recipients.
Punitive pain repeats the focus consequence inside the gratitude contrast.
Force and hardness reproduce the focus adjective as the contrast's emphatic endpoint.
Self-sufficiency blocks any reading in which punishment replenishes a needy owner.

structural_cues: 14:7 repeats the focus roots ك ف ر, ع ذ ب, and ش د د in the same warning sequence.
14:8 places even universal terrestrial kufr beside God's self-sufficiency and praiseworthiness.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies benefit-recognition, increase, kufr, the repeated severe-punishment clause, and divine self-sufficiency; I infer a recipient-side economy in which covered benefit closes into judgment. The punishment could alternatively be read as a legal consequence without a blocked-increase mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The sovereign punishes disbelief as an offense against His rule.
changed_reading.after: The self-sufficient giver judges receivers who cover benefit and refuse its growth; the severity exposes their failed reception rather than supplying anything God lacks.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later punishment forces a drinking event but replaces potable sweetness with corrupt liquid, then blocks smooth passage through the throat and ends with thick punishment. This materially realizes the baseline possibility that severe punishment is anti-refreshment held in constraint.

activation_trace.role: Sweet potable intake provides the latent positive pole that the later drink reverses.
Restraint and withholding provide the mechanism that prevents refreshment and release.
Binding supplies the held-tight quality of the failed ingestion.
Giving a drink supplies the expected act of quenching that is converted into punishment.
Ordinary water supplies the material category whose corrupted instance defeats refreshment.
Smooth passage through the throat is the bodily function explicitly denied.
The repeated punishment root closes the drinking sequence as punitive pain.
Material thickness gives the following punishment a dense and obstructive texture.

structural_cues: 14:16-17 sequences forced watering, repeated gulping, failure to swallow, death approaching from every place, and a further thick punishment.
14:17 repeats the focus punishment noun after the failed ingestion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies potable-water branches, forced drinking, denied swallowing, and thick punishment; I infer an inversion from sweetness into blocked intake. The live alternative is that the shared root's sweetness branch is only associative and the passage simply specifies one independent torment.

changed_reading.before: Severity means a generally high degree of pain.
changed_reading.after: Severity becomes an embodied anti-drink: the victim is made to ingest what cannot refresh or pass, with relief and completion continuously withheld.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus assigns every thing effectively to God; 14:18 gives the disbelievers acquired works that become fire-ash scattered by forceful wind, over which they can exercise no capacity. Possession is thus not just title but retained efficacy, sharply contrasted with acquisition that cannot be held.

activation_trace.role: The deity remains the focus possessor against whom failed human acquisition is measured.
Ash left by burning supplies an acquired product with no stable cohesion.
Force and hardness are transferred from the focus warning to the wind's destructive pressure.
Moving air supplies the carrier that removes the works from human control.
A severe wind that makes things light and scatters them provides the dispossession operation.
Capacity to act and possess is the exact efficacy denied to the disbelievers.
Acquiring benefit supplies the human claim that the ash image renders non-retainable.

structural_cues: The focus says 'to Him belongs whatever'; 14:18 says the disbelievers have no capacity over anything from what they acquired.
14:18 explicitly identifies its ash simile with those who disbelieved in their Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exhaustive divine possession and failed capacity over scattered acquisitions; I infer a rhetorical contrast between effective ownership and nominal earning. The ash simile could alternatively address only the value of works, without developing the focus possession formula.

changed_reading.before: God owns all things as a universal legal fact.
changed_reading.after: God's possession is effective retention, while the coverers' supposedly acquired results become particulate and unholdable; even their own gains cannot function as property before Him.

context_deltas.mechanism: All parties emerge exposed before God, and the false caller denies having coercive authority, disavows their association, and cannot rescue them from punishment. The focus ownership claim therefore denies not only rival title but any transferable patronage: the supposed partner abandons those who treated him as one.

activation_trace.role: The sole worshiped center anchors the contrast with a claimant who admits having no authority.
Emergence and exposure remove the social coverings under which false patronage operated.
Power and delegated authority name precisely what the false caller denies possessing.
Disavowal and renunciation turn kufr back from the followers onto their imagined patron.
Association with God supplies the false ownership arrangement that is repudiated.
Punitive pain is what the collapsed patronage cannot avert.

structural_cues: 14:21 gathers everyone before God and stages the weak asking their former superiors for relief.
14:22 moves from denied authority to mere invitation, self-blame, mutual inability to rescue, disavowal of association, and punishment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies universal exposure, denied authority, association, disavowal, and failed rescue; I infer that sole possession entails the collapse of rival patronage. A live alternative treats Satan's speech as moral blame-allocation without developing ownership.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers deny God's ownership by entertaining rivals.
changed_reading.after: Their rival arrangement has no actual authority or rescue-capacity and ends in reciprocal disavowal; sole ownership means no false patron can carry them out of the warning.

context_deltas.mechanism: The heavens-earth pair becomes one vertical growth medium: a sound word roots, holds, and branches upward, while a corrupt word is extracted from above the earth and has no settlement. God's possession is therefore an ordered field that tests whether speech can join lower foundation to upper reach.

activation_trace.role: Height supplies the upper reach into which a valid branch can grow.
Fertile planted ground supplies the lower medium in which a valid root can hold.
A trunked tree gives the word a living vertical body.
The root and base supply attachment to the lower domain.
Durable stability makes attachment persist rather than merely touch.
A high branch issuing from its root carries the grounded word toward heaven.
The explicit upper location completes the earth-to-height axis.
Total extraction from the root supplies the corrupt word's loss of attachment.
The lower counterfield becomes the surface from which the corrupt tree is removed.
Stability and settlement name the condition the uprooted word lacks.

structural_cues: 14:24 maps root, fixedness, branch, and sky in one upward simile.
14:26 reverses the mapping through extraction from above the earth and explicit lack of settlement; 14:27 then repeats stabilization.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a complete earth-to-sky growth axis and its uprooted inverse; I infer that the focus pair names a functional medium for moral-semantic stability. The alternative is that the tree simile illustrates speech without revising the earlier ownership formula.

changed_reading.before: Heavens and earth are two containers that enumerate God's property.
changed_reading.after: They are also a joined vertical field in which words either root below and reach above or lose all attachment and settlement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The coverers substitute kufr for God's benefit, settle their people in ruin, and install counterparts to divert from His road. Inside the focus's exhaustive ownership, this is an impossible exchange: a received good is replaced by its covering, then derivative beings are assigned a parity the total claim leaves no room for.

activation_trace.role: Covering benefit supplies the focus act that the later exchange makes explicit.
One thing standing in another's place supplies the corrupted exchange operation.
Good condition and benefit provide the valuable term removed by the exchange.
Ingratitude becomes the replacement term rather than merely a reaction to the benefit.
Ruin and corruption supply the household destination produced by the exchange.
A contrary counterpart supplies the rival status inserted into sole possession.
The extended road is the owned course from which the rival arrangement diverts.

structural_cues: 14:28 grammatically places God's benefit and kufr on opposite sides of a substitution.
14:28-30 sequences exchange, communal settlement in ruin, hell, rival counterparts, path-diversion, and a final return to fire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies substitution, benefit, kufr, ruin, counterparts, and diversion; I infer a failed exchange and rival title inside exhaustive possession. An alternative reading treats benefit-exchange and idolatry as two related offenses without a common property mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Disbelievers fail to acknowledge the owner of the cosmos.
changed_reading.after: They actively replace the owner's benefit with its covering and assign parity to entities already inside His possession, turning reception into ruin and return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later creation passage turns owned contents into a service network: upper water descends, lower growth emerges as allotted provision, ships and rivers are directed to human purposes, and celestial cycles remain at work. The shift from 'to Him' in the focus to repeated 'for you' means divine possession enables entrusted use; kufr covers a benefit system that is operating around the recipient.

activation_trace.role: Creative origination makes the owner the source of the network rather than a later claimant.
The overhead sky and what overshadows provide the network's upper reservoir.
Fertile planted ground provides the receiving and productive lower field.
Caused descent and delivery provide the vertical transfer between the two domains.
Water supplies the transferable material that activates the lower field.
Bringing something out of concealment supplies emergence of produce from the watered ground.
Ripe fruit supplies the network's visible productive output.
Allotted giving makes the output an assigned provision rather than ownerless yield.
Directing things toward a purpose turns possession into usable transport and flow.
Benefit and good condition collect the network's outputs under the category of gift.
Intensive covering of benefit names the human failure after the network is enumerated.

structural_cues: 14:32 repeats the focus heavens-earth pair, then narrates water, fruit, provision, ships, sea, and rivers as one causal sequence.
14:32-33 repeatedly says 'for you,' while 14:34 moves from total giving to uncountable benefit and intensive kufr.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies creation, vertical transfer, emergence, allotted provision, directed service, benefit, and kufr; I infer that ownership is exercised as provisioning and entrusted usability. The alternative is a sign-list whose repeated 'for you' indicates benefaction without implying a stewardship relation.

changed_reading.before: Whatever exists in the heavens and earth is a static inventory belonging to God.
changed_reading.after: His possession is an active provisioning network whose owned elements are directed for human use, making kufr the covering of an operating and uncountable benefit system.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same earth-sky totality later sits under an explicit denial that anything can be hidden from God, paired with concealed and declared human acts. The cover image of kufr thus loses even its apparent epistemic success: covering may obstruct a human response, but it cannot make its object or agent absent to the owner.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the attempted concealment whose effectiveness is tested.
Hiddenness and concealment name both the human act and the state denied before God.
Manifest declaration supplies the opposite pole, showing both poles are equally known.
The lower domain carries the no-hidden-thing claim across the focus field.
The overhead domain completes the same exhaustive field under epistemic transparency.

structural_cues: 14:38 first contrasts what humans conceal and declare, then denies that any thing in earth or sky is hidden from God.
The focus order heavens-earth is reversed to earth-sky while preserving exhaustive scope.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covering, concealment, declaration, and a no-hidden-thing claim across the same domains; I infer that ownership includes complete exposure. The alternative is that 14:38 concerns knowledge alone and does not feed back into the semantic force of kufr.

changed_reading.before: The coverers successfully suppress acknowledgment even though God owns the field.
changed_reading.after: Their covering can deform reception but cannot conceal any act, object, or interior state from the owner of the entire field.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final scene does not merely rearrange things within heavens and earth; earth itself stands in for another earth, the heavens are included in the replacement, and all emerge exposed before the one overpowering God. The focus owner therefore possesses not only all contents but the contingency of their containers.

activation_trace.role: One thing standing in another's place supplies replacement of the cosmic field itself.
The lower domain appears on both sides of replacement, making the container contingent.
The upper canopy joins the lower domain as an object of cosmic replacement.
Emergence and exposure strip every contained being of shelter during the transition.
Divine oneness without partner preserves the owner while both domains change.
Overpowering from above supplies the efficacy by which exposed contents and containers submit.

structural_cues: 14:48 reuses both focus domain nouns but moves from 'whatever is in' them to replacement of the domains themselves.
The replacement clause leads directly into universal emergence before the one overpowering God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies replacement of earth and heavens, exposure, oneness, and overpowering; I infer that the focus title includes power over the containers, not only their contents. The alternative is that the final scene specifies eschatological change without expanding the earlier grammar of possession.

changed_reading.before: God owns everything located inside a stable heavens-and-earth cosmos.
changed_reading.after: Even the cosmic coordinates are contingent holdings: their contents, their boundaries, and their replacement remain before the one owner who persists.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing punishment binds bodies together in fetters, clothes them in tar, and lets fire cover their faces before each self is repaid for what it acquired. The focus roots become a material reciprocity: those characterized by covering are themselves covered, while severity's fastening image becomes literal restraint.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the initiating human operation that returns as an enveloping punishment.
Fastening and binding supply the latent material shape of severity.
Joining one thing to another and binding it supplies collective restraint.
Tight bonds and fetters concretize the focus adjective as immobilizing force.
A human garment supplies a body-scale layer of punitive enclosure.
Viscous tar supplies the material coating of the punitive garment.
A cover that rises over and conceals its object reverses kufr's covering onto the coverers' faces.
Matching action with its recompense supplies the explicit reciprocity behind the reversal.
Acquired action identifies what the recompense answers rather than an arbitrary target.

structural_cues: 14:49-50 moves from paired binding to fetters, clothing, coating, and fire covering the face.
14:51 immediately states that every self is recompensed for what it acquired.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies coverers, fastening severity, bonds, coating, covering fire, and action-matched recompense; I infer a cover-for-cover reversal. The live alternative is that the closing images are punitive specifications without intentional lexical reciprocity with kufr.

changed_reading.before: Covering truth leads to an unspecified severe penalty.
changed_reading.after: The penalty mirrors and materializes the act: coverers are fastened, coated, and covered, with severity becoming a bodily bond and recompense matching acquisition.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's alternate و س م mapping for the focus spelling rather than the ordinary sky branch. It remains anchored because that mapped branch explicitly images first rain marking earth with vegetation, and 14:32 performs exactly a sky-water-to-fruit sequence. Downstream prose should present it as branch-triggered wordplay or an inscription analogy, not as the lexical translation of 'heavens.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus's س م و inventory includes an alternate mapped branch in which first rain marks earth with vegetation; the same focus also names fertile earth and coverers of benefit.

activation_trace.role: First rain marking earth with plants supplies a latent image of the upper domain inscribing the lower one.
Fertile planted earth supplies the receptive surface on which the rain-mark appears.
Covering benefit supplies the human attempt to obscure the resulting visible mark.
The repeated upper source reactivates the branch image precisely where rain descends.
Water provides the marking medium carried from upper to lower field.
Emergence from concealment makes the rain's mark visible as produced growth.
Ripe fruit supplies the legible outcome of the water-mark.
Benefit gathers the rain-written growth under the gift that kufr covers.

changed_reading.before: The heavens and earth are visible property, while kufr denies the owner's claim.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the upper domain writes the owner's benefit onto fertile earth in rain and fruit, so kufr is an attempt to cover a materially inscribed gift.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the focus noun ordinarily denotes disbelief, not farming. It remains anchored in the packet's explicit seed-covering branch for ك ف ر and is activated by the sustained tree, root, earth, branch, and uprooting mechanism in 14:24-26. Downstream prose should call it an agricultural irony, never redefine the disbelievers as farmers or claim direct etymological exegesis.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus's ك ف ر inventory includes covering seed with earth, while the surah later tests words as rooted or uprooted trees across earth and sky.

activation_trace.role: Covering seed with soil supplies the productive counterpart that makes the coverers' sterility ironic.
Fertile planted earth supplies the proper medium in which covering should enable growth.
The trunked tree supplies the mature result expected from productive planting.
The root and base provide the successful attachment missing from corrupt covering.
Durable fixedness supplies the sign that the covered seed has entered a viable order.
The high branch issuing from the root supplies the productive upward result.
Complete uprooting supplies the failed agricultural outcome that reverses productive covering.

changed_reading.before: Kufr's covering image is uniformly concealment and negation.
changed_reading.after: The tree sequence creates an agricultural irony: covering can nurture a seed into rooted ascent, but these coverers produce the opposite condition, a word-growth torn from earth with no stability.

strongest_changes: The exact recurrence in 14:7-8 turns severe punishment into the recipient-side consequence of covering benefit while explicitly excluding divine need.
The tree sequence and the creation-provision sequence turn heavens and earth from static containers into a vertical growth field and an active service network.
14:48 extends ownership from everything inside the cosmos to the replaceability of earth and heavens themselves.
14:49-51 materializes the focus roots in reciprocal form: coverers are bound, coated, and covered as each self is repaid for what it acquired.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence repeatedly changed the focus from an abstract sovereignty-warning into a set of mechanisms: extraction from covering, gratitude and increase, failed acquisition, rooted speech, provisioned use, cosmic replacement, and cover-for-cover recompense. The packet's alternate rain-mark branch added a contained but unusually exact ecological activation.
remaining_uncertainties: The potable-sweetness and withholding branches of ع ذ ب may be associative activations rather than components of the punishment noun in context.
The و س م rain-inscription reading is visibly packet-licensed but remains form-distant and should not displace the ordinary sky reading.
The cover-for-cover relation between ك ف ر and the fire covering faces may be rhetorical reciprocity supplied by the reader rather than an intended lexical echo.
The provisioning network clearly marks benefaction, but its stronger implication of entrusted use remains inferential.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Cosmic possession makes concealment a withholding of what is already encompassed.** `ك ف ر` `B001` (covering/concealment) and `B004` (covering over a favor) stand between `س م و` `B004` (overhead cover) and `ء ر ض` `B001` (lower ground), while `ش د د` `B001` adds a tightened bond. Later enumeration of rain, fruit, ships, rivers, sun, moon, night, and day fills out what “belongs.” I infer that rejection constricts the beneficiary's relation to an all-encompassing gift-order; the punishment is read as the severe tightening of a covered favor, not an unrelated penalty.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayat 14:32–34 filled the initially abstract heaven-earth possession with a working inventory, making concealment of favor a denial of interdependent systems rather than isolated gifts.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The vertical pair defines an enclosing jurisdiction.** `س م و B004` supplies the overhead sky or cover, and `ء ر ض B001` the lower ground opposite it. Their balanced `فِى ... وَمَا فِى ...` construction fills the space from cover to floor. I infer from that packet-supplied spatial totality that `لَهُ` denotes jurisdiction throughout an enclosure, so the claim reads as comprehensive spatial governance rather than a list of two possessions.
2. **The unbelievers are specifically favor-coverers.** `ك ف ر B004` supplies covering over a favor. Within the forward half of the focus window, 14:5 names signs, 14:6 names divine favor, and 14:7 directly opposes gratitude to kufr. The packet supplies that lexical progression; I infer that it specifies the relevant object being covered in 14:2. `لِّلْكَافِرِينَ` thus acquires the sharper reading “those who occlude acknowledged benefaction,” alongside rejection of truth (`ك ف ر B003`).
3. **Severity is a firmly attached consequence.** Besides intensity (`ش د د B002`), `ش د د B001` supplies fastening a bond. The paired conditional clauses of 14:7 repeat `عَذَاب` and `شَدِيد` after the favor/gratitude sequence, giving punishment a tightly coupled condition. The conditional linkage is supplied; I infer the fastening arrow. `عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ` can therefore read as punishment firmly bound to sustained covering, not intensity alone.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:7 supplied the surprise by placing gratitude, kufr, punishment, and `شَدِيد` in one balanced conditional. That later construction activated favor-covering (`ك ف ر B004`) and the firmly attached consequence (`ش د د B001`).

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tapınma eylemini, kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini, bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı ve tapınılan varlığı aynı anlam örgüsü içinde açıkça birleştirir. Geçici dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği ve ondan türeyen varlık adlarını doğru biçimde temsil eder.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, tapınma eylemi ile bundan türeyen tapınılan veya tapınılır kılınan varlık anlamlarını kapsar; şaşkınlık, yoğun üzüntü ve salt özel ad kullanımları bu sınırın dışındadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, tapınmayı anlamın temeli sayar; kişinin tapınmaya yönelmesini, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınılır kılma işlemini bu temelden türetir. Tapınma konusu sayılan yontular ve güneş örneği, varlık anlamının belirli uygulamalarıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir varlığı tapınma konusu durumuna getirme işlemini korur.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أله وتأله بمعنى عبد وتنسك، والتأليه بمعنى التعبيد، والإله والآلهة والإلاهة لما جعل معبودا.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه أله بمعنى تحير، ولا ألهت على فلان بمعنى اشتد جزعي عليه، ولا أسماء المواضع أو الحية أو الهلال إلا من جهة التسمية لا معنى العبادة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو التعبد، فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود، وتأله الرجل إذا تعبد، والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها (maqayis)؛ التأله التعبد (ayn)؛ أله بالفتح إلاهة أي عبد عبادة، مألوه أي معبود، الآلهة الأصنام، التأليه التعبيد، التأله التنسك والتعبد (sihah)؛ لا يكون إلاها حتى يكون معبودا، معبوداتهم من الأصنام والأوثان آلهة، الإلاهة الشمس، وإلاهتك وعبادتك (tahdhib)؛ إله اسما لكل معبود، أله فلان يأله الآلهة عبد، فالإله على هذا هو المعبود (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini, genel tapınılan-varlık adından türetiliş açıklamasını ve bu özel adla kurulan seslenme ile ant biçimlerini birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve kullanılabilir, ancak dal yalnızca seslenme ve ant kalıpları değildir; özel adın yalın kullanımı da çekirdekte tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, özel ad ile bu ada bağlı seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimleriyle sınırlıdır; herhangi bir tapınılan varlığı gösteren genel ad anlamına genişletilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın özel ad, doğrudan seslenme biçimleri ve ant ya da şaşma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplara özgü işlevler özel adın her kullanımına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini ve bu adla kurulan seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimlerini kapsar. Bu biçimler doğrudan seslenme, adın ant değeriyle kullanılması veya ses ve parçaların düşürülmesiyle kısaltılma yollarını gösterir.

facets.statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
Özel adın, tapınılan varlığı bildiren genel addan ses düşmesi ve belirleyici unsur eklenmesiyle oluştuğu açıklanır.
Özel ad, sözün başında ant değeri taşıyarak ardından gelen yapmama bildirimini güçlendirebilir.
Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak cümlesi üstte bulunup örten şey çekirdeğini gök ve tavanla verir; bulut, yağmur, bitki, atın sırtı ve her şeyin üst yanı kullanımlarını da açıkça ekler. Dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği ve ona bağlı aktarmaları doğru ayırmaya elverişlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin üzerinde bulunan ve onu örten gök, tavan ya da genel üst yandır. Bu ad buluta, yukarıdan gelen yağmura, yağmurla çıkan veya yükselen bitkiye ve atın sırtına da aktarılır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin üzerinde yükselen ve onu örten gök, tavan veya üst yan anlatılır.
Üstte bulunan ve örten bulut aynı adla anılır.
Yukarıdaki kaynağından gelen yağmur aynı adla anılır.
Yağmurdan çıkan veya yerden yükselen bitkiye aynı ad aktarılır.
Atın sırtı ve genel olarak bir şeyin en üst yanı bu yüksek üst yüzey kapsamında adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar gök, tavan ve üst yan anlamlarını yüksekte bulunup örtme çekirdeğinde birleştirir; bulut, yağmur, bitki ve at sırtı kullanımlarını buna bağlı uzantılar olarak verir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi tanıtan ad, bu adı verme veya edinme ve başka biriyle aynı adı taşıma ilişkisidir. Ayrıca aynı adı ya da niteliği hak edecek ölçüde denk olmayı anlatır; kaynaklar adlandırmayı anılmayı yükseltme düşüncesiyle açıklar.

Taraflardan biri ötekine karşı koyar, onunla aynı düzeye gelmeye veya onu geçmeye çalışır.
Kimsenin bir kişiyle yarışamaması, o kişinin erişilemez ölçüde üstün olduğunu bildirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi ya da hayvanı tanınmasını sağlayacak görünür bir izle işaretleme eylemini, bu eylemin bıraktığı izi ve işaretlemede kullanılan kızgın aracı birlikte verir. Sağlanan dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her türlü soyut belirtiyi değil; yakma, kulak kesme veya çentikleme gibi yollarla bırakılan tanıtıcı fiziksel izi kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, ortak fiziksel işaretleme çekirdeğiyle sınırlıdır; zırhın alt bölümündeki süslemeyi anlatan özel tamlama yalnızca kendi sözlüksel karşılığında korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi ya da hayvanı, tanınmasını veya ayırt edilmesini sağlayan kalıcı ve görünür bir fiziksel iz oluşturacak biçimde işaretlemektir; iz yakma, kulak kesme ya da çentikleme yoluyla bırakılabilir. Anlam alanı, oluşan işareti ve özellikle hayvanı işaretlemeye yarayan kızgın aracı da kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesne veya hayvan üzerinde onu tanıtmaya ve başkalarından ayırmaya yarayan görünür bir fiziksel iz oluşturulur.
İşaret, kızgın araçla yakılarak, kulağın bir bölümü kesilerek veya çentik açılarak bırakılabilir.
Eylemin sonucunda kalan tanıtıcı iz de aynı anlam alanında adlandırılır.
Özellikle hayvanlara bu izi koymak için kullanılan kızgın işaretleme aracı da bu dala bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatımda temel ilişki, tanınacak şey üzerinde kasıtlı ve kalıcı bir iz oluşturma ilişkisidir. Yakma, kulak kesme ve çentikleme bu işlemin yollarıdır; sonuçtaki iz ile onu koyan kızgın araç da anlam alanına dahildir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişide görülen belirtiyi okuyarak iyilik, kötülük veya genel durum hakkında sonuç çıkarma eylemini açıkça anlatır. Dal çerçevesindeki bakma, belirti ve çıkarım ilişkisi bu anlamı doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Burada belirtiyi yalnızca görmek yetmez; görünür izden kişinin niteliği veya durumu hakkında çıkarım yapılması gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, kişideki belirtiyi yorumlama çekirdeğini verir; iyilik veya kötülükle kurulan özel yapılar bu çekirdeğin bağlama bağlı gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişide görülen belirti veya izlere dikkatle bakarak onun iyiliği, kötülüğü, niteliği ya da durumu hakkında sezgisel bir sonuca varmaktır. Anlam, belirtinin kendisinden çok onu okuyup görünmeyen bir niteliği çıkarma eylemine dayanır.

facets.statement: Kişide görülen bir belirti, görünmeyen bir nitelik veya durumun göstergesi olarak okunur.
Gözlemden hareketle sezgisel bir değerlendirme ve çıkarım yapılır.
Çıkarılan nitelik iyilik de kötülük de olabilir; anlam yalnızca olumlu bir yargıyla sınırlı değildir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, kişideki görünür bir izin onun iyiliğine, kötülüğüne veya durumuna işaret ettiğini fark etmek ve bu işaretten sezgisel bir sonuç çıkarmaktır. Bakan kişi, belirtiyi anlam taşıyan bir gösterge olarak değerlendirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişideki görünür işaretten onun görünmeyen niteliği hakkında çıkarım yapma çekirdeğinin tamamında kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Belirtiyi gözlemleme, onu gösterge sayma ve kişilik ya da durum hakkında sonuç çıkarma aşamalarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Görünür belirtilerin okunması ve bunlardan bir kişinin durumu hakkında sonuç çıkarılması vurgulandığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Gözlenen belirtileri anlamlı göstergeler olarak yorumlama ve sonuç çıkarma sürecini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişideki belirtilerden onun iyiliği, kötülüğü veya genel niteliği hakkında hızlı bir yargıya varıldığında doğaldır.
